audit.whatIsWrong: Six of seven rows disagreed with the packet chart, and several disagreed with their own why text: Level 1 was called even though the why says Ornn out-tempos him, Levels 2, 3 and the first-item row were given to Ornn though their whys all say 'even', and Level 6 was called even though its why calls it Ornn's cleanest kill window.
audit.why: Infected Bonesaw only pokes at level 1; through 3-5 he simply walks off and heals, which is a standoff, not an Ornn win; level 6 is the one stage his pre-item healing cannot outrun a chained knockup.
audit.corrected: Whole chart proposed as one atomic group in matched pairs — Ornn, Skill, Skill, Skill, Ornn, Skill, Skill — which is the packet chart except the 2+ items row, set to Skill to match the mirror. Ratings and the full whys moved with it, and content whys[6] rewritten so it no longer claims he reclaims the stage outright.

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[4].why, phases[5].why and phases[6].why were all boilerplate and named no spike.
audit.why: Level 6 is Call of the Forge God against a Mundo who has not stacked health yet. The first-item stage is where his health item turns his sustain on. Late, Maximum Dosage (120s, heals a percent of missing health) wins him the duel while Ornn's Masterwork upgrades win the fight.
audit.corrected: All three rewritten to name the spike and its owner.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page never mentioned Goes Where He Pleases — his passive resists the first immobilising effect that hits him. Against a champion whose whole pattern is knockup-into-Brittle, that is the single most important interaction in the matchup, and it was absent from both layers. Heart Zapper's stored-damage heal, Maximum Dosage's missing-health heal and Blunt Force Trauma's auto-reset tell were also missing.
audit.why: If the passive is up, the first knockup is simply cancelled and he drops a cannister that heals him when he walks over it. The correct play is to spend a cheap CC first and land the real chain on the second one.
audit.corrected: breakdown.cooldowns leads with the passive and the throwaway-CC rule; tradeGood now opens by baiting the cannister; the dontsFull bodies carry Bonesaw's 4s/975, the two healing sources and the missing-health scaling.

edits.before: Q-poke and AA-trade — your base stats are quietly elite. Identify how Dr. Mundo contests the first waves before you commit anything.
edits.after: Mundo is one of the weakest level 1s and Infected Bonesaw only pokes — deny last-hits and take the tempo while he is weak.

edits.before: W brittle turns every trade into bonus %HP damage. Only take the trade when Dr. Mundo's Heart Zapper is down.
edits.after: Neither of you has a combo — he tosses Bonesaw to sustain, you farm; there is no kill pressure at 2.

edits.before: Full kit online — your core pattern starts now. Keep the wave near your side so Dr. Mundo must walk into your engage range.
edits.after: Bellows Breath answers his Bonesaw poke, but he walks off and heals through it, so the trade math stays roughly even.

edits.before: Call of the Forge God re-engages a whole fight — and your forge prints item leads. Reassess every all-in at 6 — Dr. Mundo's ultimate changes the math too.
edits.after: Call of the Forge God's charge and recast knockup chain enough burst to beat his pre-item healing — your cleanest kill window before he stacks health.

edits.before: Iceborn Gauntlet is your spike — force fights the moment it completes, on Heart Zapper's cooldown.
edits.after: His first health item turns his sustain on as yours completes — trades go spongey and even.

edits.before: Two items on: your side-lane pattern is at full power. Dr. Mundo carry threat 8/10 — close before the map decides instead of you.
edits.after: He reclaims the side-lane 1v1 with Maximum Dosage, but your Masterwork upgrades and chain CC own the 5v5 — even overall.

edits.before: His R Maximum Dosage heal makes him unkillable 1v1 and he out-itemizes your single-target CC — the drain-tank reclaims the duel late.
edits.after: His Maximum Dosage heal wins him the 1v1, but your Masterwork upgrades and teamfight CC keep this stage even overall.

edits.before: - Dr. Mundo Heart Zapper: matchup-defining — His sustain + reset. Anti-heal it. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Goes Where He Pleases: his passive eats your first immobilise — spend a throwaway CC before the real knockup. - Heart Zapper: 17s, heals off stored damage. - Infected Bonesaw: 4s, 975 range. - Maximum Dosage: 120s.

edits.before: His sustain + reset. Anti-heal it. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: Heart Zapper is 17s and heals off stored damage — trade on its downtime.

edits.before: That is Dr. Mundo's favourite window — refuse it and half his win condition is gone.
edits.after: Infected Bonesaw is 4s at 975 range and scales on your current health — step aside.

edits.before: Burning it for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown.
edits.after: Heart Zapper and Maximum Dosage both heal — Grievous Wounds early.

edits.before: E-dashing with no terrain in the line — no knockup means you delivered yourself to his combo for free.
edits.after: Maximum Dosage heals a percent of missing health, so the longer the brawl runs the worse it gets.

edits.before: Q the pillar behind Dr. Mundo, E-dash through it for the knockup when his answer is down, and W-brittle the trade for the proc.
edits.after: Bait his passive cannister with a cheap knockup first, then Q the pillar, Searing Charge into it, and W to Brittle him.

notes: The biggest gap on this page was Goes Where He Pleases: his passive resists the first immobilising effect, which is exactly what Ornn's whole pattern is made of, and neither layer mentioned it. The 2+ items row was set to Skill to match the mirror rather than to the packet's 'Dr. Mundo', since the two directions must agree. Data discrepancy flagged by the mirror and still present: this brief's header says games 1844 while the mirror's packet reported 900 for the same matchup — worth checking which figure the page renders. Not asserted: exactly how Brittle is consumed, which Riot's text does not state.
